newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden gov sees 12 bln Skr 88 budget surplus - radio.
newsitem.headline: Sweden gov sees 12 bln Skr 88 budget surplus - radio.

text.p: Sweden's 1998 budget was expected to show a surplus of up to 12 billion crowns against previous estimates of 10 billion crowns, according to a budget leak reported by Swedish radio on Wednesday.
The minority Social Democratic government therefore has more money than planned to spend on combatting unemployment, Swedish National Radio's Ekot show said.
In February, Swedish unemployment stood at 8.8 percent, according to Statistics Sweden data. Prime Minister Goran Persson has pledged to halve unemployment to four percent by the year 2000.

In its spring budget proposal, due to be released on April 15, the government will give support to small companies by lifting the wages level at which employers have to pay fees to the state for their staff, the radio said.
Currently small companies pay lower fees for staff who wages are under 600,000 crowns a year but the government will propose to raise this sum to 800,000 crowns.

Other budget measures are the option of early retirement for older staff, room for 15,000 new university students, a proposal for a new trainee system and several large construction projects, the radio said.
The government has also been forced to scale down its plans for large cuts on dental care expenses and will not cut back on personal assistants for the disabled, the radio said.
